openings.claim: Padded removable strip stops could resist sideways movement while straps provide minimal seating preload, avoiding the asymmetric compression implicated in opposite-corner lift.
openings.delta: Separate lateral registration from separation restraint instead of treating tighter seal compression as sufficient retention.
openings.prediction: If reversible stop attachment is feasible, ten closures including the right-contact card closure will retain position within 1 mm during and after 20 N, reopen within 30 seconds, and leave no new visible seal tears.
openings.probe: First check reversible attachment and full opening clearance. Fabricate only with supplied resources. Use ten closure/pull trials, disturbing the tenth. Record marked displacement before, during and after pull, corner lift, reopening time and seal condition. Any outcome failure defeats this configuration; continuous disturbed seal contact is exempt.
assumptions: Existing rim geometry permits removable padded stops and strap attachment without permanent modification.
Supplied strip, bolt and strap dimensions accommodate that attachment.

openings.claim: A friction-dependent closure may appear centered after unloading while exceeding the position tolerance under load, particularly with the disturbed contact.
openings.delta: Distinguish loaded movement from residual drift; a contact mark or unloaded position cannot establish resistance to the specified pull.
openings.prediction: A feasible strap-only comparator will show greater loaded displacement than residual displacement, with the right-contact card potentially worsening the difference.
openings.probe: Allocate the remaining two permitted closure/pull trials to the comparator, one centered and one disturbed. Measure before, during and after the same 20 N pull. No loaded/residual difference defeats the prediction; passing two trials does not establish ten-cycle success. Abort any attachment that violates constraints.
assumptions: A reversible strap-only comparator can be assembled from supplied resources.

assessment: These are untested hypotheses. Twelve shared pull trials cover two configurations and both disturbances; only the stop configuration receives ten-cycle qualification. If reversible attachments are infeasible, no construction opening is supported. Stipulated observations establish neither efficacy nor attachment geometry.
